blocks.text: If you write press releases and pitches on a Mac, Google Docs is probably already open in a tab. Google's help pages describe Docs as a web app. I found no separate Google Docs app for Mac. This guide shows how to set up Docs in the browser, start from templates, review drafts, and work offline. It ends with where Lazur fits while you write.
Set up Google Docs in the right browser on your Mac

Google's screen reader help page says the editors should be used as a web application instead of a web page. It recommends the latest Chrome browser. Start there. Open Chrome, go to docs.google.com, and sign in with the account your firm uses for client work.

items: Update Chrome first. Choose Chrome > About Google Chrome, and let it finish before you open a draft.
Use your work account. Google says some template features are only available for work or school accounts.
Press ⌘ / inside a document to open the keyboard shortcut popup.
Press ⌘ ⌥ Z only if you use a screen reader. It turns screen reader support on or off.
Pin Docs as a tab, so your draft folder is one click away when a reporter calls back.

blocks.text: Browser choice matters again later, when you work offline. For every other task in this guide, Chrome is the safe default. Stick with it, and most surprises go away.
Start a press release from a Google Docs template

Google's template steps start at the menu bar. Choose File > New > From a template. Scroll the gallery, select a template, and click Insert. The template gives you the layout. It does not know your client's boilerplate, approved quotes, or the house style your editors expect.

Build one master copy of your own release. Keep it in a shared Drive folder, and set it to view only, so no one edits it by accident. For each new announcement, make a copy of the master and rename it with the client and the launch. The steps are at /how-to/make-a-copy-of-a-document-in-google-docs.
Fix the template problems that waste your morning
Templates behave differently depending on what is already in your document. Google's template page covers the main case. The table lists what you will hit, and the fix for each one.

rows: The template opens as a new document from the gallery
Insert the template, then paste your release text into the layout
The template opens in new document tabs
Look for the new tab at the top of the window, then copy only what you need
Some template features only work for work or school accounts
Switch to your firm's account before you build a shared template
You want to share a custom template
Google's template help page does not describe custom template sharing
Keep a master copy in a shared folder and copy it for each release
blocks.caption: Template problems you will hit, and what to do about each one.

blocks.text: The last row matters most for agencies. A gallery template is a starting point. Your own master copy does more work, because it carries the facts your clients approved last time.
Review pitches with Suggesting mode and comments

Clients and editors often want to mark changes, not rewrite your draft. Use Suggesting mode for tracked edits, and use comments for questions. Switch modes with the editing mode control, which sits near the Share button. In Suggesting mode, each change you type appears as a proposed edit that the other person can accept or reject.

Comments need a clear anchor. Select the sentence first, then press ⌘ ⌥ M. Ask one question per comment, so the reply stays easy to follow. The exact clicks for each step live in /how-to/suggest-edits-in-google-docs and /how-to/add-a-comment-in-google-docs.
Use Gemini in Docs to refine a paragraph

Gemini in Docs starts from the Gemini icon. Click it, type a prompt, and you do not need to select any text. Gemini reads the context of your document. To change one paragraph, select it, then click Refine on the floating bar. The options are Rephrase, Shorten, Elaborate, More formal, More casual, Bulletize, and Summarize.

Gemini suggestions show up in the document itself. Click Accept suggestion to apply one change at a time. Use Accept all or Reject all when the whole pass looks right or wrong. Read every rewrite before you accept it, especially sentences with quotes, names and figures.

Two details trip people up. The Gemini bar minimizes by default, so hover over Gemini to bring it back. And the feature requires an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. Writing-style matching is only available through Workspace Experiments for personal accounts.

blocks.title: Check your plan first
blocks.text: Gemini depends on your Google plan, not your Mac. If the feature is missing on a deadline day, check your account before you blame Chrome or Lazur.
Google Docs offline on Mac: what works and what does not

Offline editing needs Chrome or Edge. Google's offline help page says you must use one of those browsers. Edge users get sent to the Chrome Web Store for the Google Docs Offline extension. Safari is not on that list. Private browsing does not support offline access, and only one account per browser profile can have it turned on.

The offline page never mentions macOS. It names ChromeOS as the only platform where offline turns on automatically. On a Mac, you set it up yourself. The Chrome steps are at /how-to/turn-on-offline-mode-in-google-docs.
Open each file once while you are online, so it is ready when the signal drops. Do this the night before a trip, not in the taxi to the airport.
Where Lazur fits while you write in Google Docs

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click for you. It does not edit your files or operate other apps. It points, explains, answers, and types text when you ask. That split suits Docs well. You keep control of the draft, and Lazur keeps you out of the menus.

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app, including Docs. Snippets help with the parts you repeat, such as your contact block. A personal dictionary keeps client surnames spelled the way you want them.
Things to say to Lazur while you draft

Most questions in Docs fall into three groups. You need to find something, learn a menu path, or get a sentence drafted. The examples in this guide use plain speech. Say them the way you would ask a colleague across the desk.

Name the thing you mean. Say the Gemini icon, not that thing on the right. Lazur looks at the screen, so a clear name gets you a clear circle. Vague questions get vague answers, and that is true of colleagues too.
Worked example: one launch pitch from first draft to sent
Here is one run for a product launch pitch, start to finish. The client has a named spokesperson, a fixed embargo date, and a short list of target outlets. The steps keep the work in one file.

items: Make a copy of your master release. Rename it with the client and the launch name.
Draft the opening in editing mode. Keep your own voice in the first two sentences.
Switch to Suggesting mode before the client reviews, so their edits are tracked.
Select the second paragraph, click Refine, and choose Shorten. Read the result before you accept it.
Click Accept suggestion on the change you want. Ask Lazur where the reject control is if you cannot find it.
Press ⌘ F and search for each date, name and number. Check every one against the brief.
Press ⌘ ⇧ C to check the word count against the outlet's length limit.
Share the file as Commenter for the client. Keep Editor access for teammates who need to change text.
Choose File > Version history > See version history, then name the version you sent.

blocks.text: Two checks catch most errors. Search for [, which shows leftover template placeholders. Then search for every number and compare each one to the source document. Treat Gemini as a rewriter, not a fact checker.
Mistakes PR specialists make in Google Docs

items: Leaving template placeholders in the final copy. Search for [ before you send anything.
Sending a client a file with Suggesting mode still on, so their view is cluttered with your own tracked changes.
Accepting Gemini rewrites without reading the numbers and quotes they touch.
Sharing with Editor access when the client only needs to read. Pick Viewer or Commenter.
Starting a template inside a document that already has text, then losing track of the new tab.
Assuming offline works in Safari. Google's offline help page names Chrome or Edge.
Saving several drafts of one release with names like final, final2. Name versions instead.

blocks.text: Why pitch writing takes so much of the week

Determ's PR Statistics 2024 article says 62% of PR professionals identify content creation, such as pitches and press releases, as their most time-consuming task. The sample was 300 participants from Determ's own survey and HARO. The article does not state the survey year. Determ is a PR vendor, so treat the number as a signal, not a benchmark.

Muck Rack's 2025 State of PR survey was fielded June 5 to July 16, 2025. It analyzed 911 qualified responses from 1,089 PR professionals. The figures below come from a syndicated release on Yahoo Finance, not the full report. 70% say they personalize pitches to some extent. Just 11% say they fully customize each pitch.

The 70% and the 11% sit side by side. That gap is where a good master copy and a short review loop help. The same release says 77% already use tools like ChatGPT in their workflow, so check every AI draft against the brief before it leaves your desk.
Share, version and sign off a client draft

Use the Share button at the top right of the document. Give clients Viewer or Commenter access. Give Editor access only to people who need to change text. Check the link setting before you paste it into an email.

Name a version before each send. Choose File > Version history > See version history, then name the current version. When a client asks what changed in round two, you can open the older version and compare.
Suggestions and versions do different jobs. A version is a snapshot of the whole file. Suggestions show individual edits inside one live draft. Use both, and your sign-off trail stays clear.
Limits to know before you rely on Lazur in Docs
Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Google Docs or any other app.
Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. If you ask where Gemini is, Lazur points. You click. That matters when a client change needs your judgment, not a shortcut.
Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
Where to go next

If you are setting up Docs for the first time, start with the template steps and the offline page above. Then run one Gemini refine on a paragraph you already wrote. For word count, see /how-to/see-word-count-in-google-docs. When you want Lazur on your Mac, get it at /download.

faq.question: Is there a Google Docs app for Mac?
faq.answer: I found no separate Google Docs app for Mac. Google's help pages describe Docs as a web app. Open docs.google.com in the latest Chrome, and keep it pinned as a tab for the work you do every day.

faq.question: Does Google Docs work offline in Safari on Mac?
faq.answer: Google's offline help page says you must use Chrome or Edge for offline editing. Safari is not on that list. If you need a draft on a plane, open it in Chrome while you are online first.

faq.question: Why did my template open in a new tab?
faq.answer: Google's template help says that if the document already has content, the template opens in new document tabs. Look for the new tab at the top of the window, then copy only the parts you need into your draft.

faq.question: Do I need a paid plan to use Gemini in Google Docs?
faq.answer: Google's Gemini help page says the feature requires an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. Check your account before a deadline. If the Gemini icon is missing, the plan is the first thing to look at.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Google Doc for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps. It points at things, explains them, answers out loud, and guides you one click at a time. You make the edits.

faq.question: How do I find every placeholder in a Google Doc on Mac?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ F and search for the left square bracket. Template placeholders often use brackets, so this finds the leftovers quickly. Then replace each one with the real detail from the brief.

faq.question: Can I dictate into Google Docs with Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app, including Docs. Use your personal dictionary for client names so they come out spelled the way you want.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows too?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available today.
